function.name: patch
function.description:
Targeted find-and-replace edits in files. Use this instead of sed/awk in terminal. Uses fuzzy matching (9 strategies) so minor whitespace/indentation differences won't break it. Returns a unified diff. Auto-runs syntax checks after editing.

REPLACE MODE (mode='replace', default): find a unique string and replace it. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: mode, path, old_string, new_string.
PATCH MODE (mode='patch'): apply V4A multi-file patches for bulk changes. REQUIRED PARAMETERS: mode, patch.

mode.description: Edit mode. 'replace' (default): requires path + old_string + new_string. 'patch': requires patch content only.

path.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. File path to edit.

old_string.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. Exact text to find and replace. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all=true. Include surrounding context lines to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: REQUIRED when mode='replace'. Replacement text. Pass empty string '' to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false)

patch.description:
REQUIRED when mode='patch'. V4A format patch content. Format:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: path/to/file
@@ context hint @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
*** End Patch

function.name: process
function.description: Manage background processes started with terminal(background=true). Actions: 'list' (show all), 'poll' (check status + new output), 'log' (full output with pagination), 'wait' (block until done or timeout), 'kill' (terminate), 'write' (send raw stdin data without newline), 'submit' (send data + Enter, for answering prompts), 'close' (close stdin/send EOF).

action.description: Action to perform on background processes

session_id.description: Process session ID (from terminal background output). Required for all actions except 'list'.

data.description: Text to send to process stdin (for 'write' and 'submit' actions)

timeout.description: Max seconds to block for 'wait' action. Returns partial output on timeout.

offset.description: Line offset for 'log' action (default: last 200 lines)

limit.description: Max lines to return for 'log' action

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

target.description: 'content' searches inside file contents, 'files' searches for files by name

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for short commands.
Background: Set background=true to get a session_id. Two patterns:
  (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers).
  (2) Long-running tasks with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working on other things and the system auto-notifies you when the task finishes. Great for test suites, builds, deployments, or anything that takes more than a minute.
For servers/watchers, do NOT use shell-level background wrappers (nohup/disown/setsid/trailing '&') in foreground mode. Use background=true so Hermes can track lifecycle and output.
After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check or log signal, then run tests in a separate terminal() call. Avoid blind sleep loops.
Use process(action="poll") for progress checks, process(action="wait") to block until done.
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: Run the command in the background. Two patterns: (1) Long-lived processes that never exit (servers, watchers). (2) Long-running tasks paired with notify_on_complete=true — you can keep working and get notified when the task finishes. For short commands, prefer foreground with a generous timeout instead.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180, foreground max: 600). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily. Foreground timeout above 600s is rejected; use background=true for longer commands.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

notify_on_complete.description: When true (and background=true), you'll be automatically notified exactly once when the process finishes. **This is the right choice for almost every long-running task** — tests, builds, deployments, multi-item batch jobs, anything that takes over a minute and has a defined end. Use this and keep working on other things; the system notifies you on exit. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with watch_patterns — when both are set, watch_patterns is dropped.

watch_patterns.description: Strings to watch for in background process output. HARD RATE LIMIT: at most 1 notification per 15 seconds per process — matches arriving inside the cooldown are dropped. After 3 consecutive 15-second windows with dropped matches, watch_patterns is automatically disabled for that process and promoted to notify_on_complete behavior (one notification on exit, no more mid-process spam). USE ONLY for truly rare, one-shot mid-process signals on LONG-LIVED processes that will never exit on their own — e.g. ['Application startup complete'] on a server so you know when to hit its endpoint, or ['migration done'] on a daemon. DO NOT use for: (1) end-of-run markers like 'DONE'/'PASS' — use notify_on_complete instead; (2) error patterns like 'ERROR'/'Traceback' in loops or multi-item batch jobs — they fire on every iteration and you'll hit the strike limit fast; (3) anything you'd ever combine with notify_on_complete. When in doubt, choose notify_on_complete. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with notify_on_complete — set one, not both.

# AI Readiness Consulting Pipeline

## Pipeline Overview
This pipeline manages the complete consulting process from initial promotion through final delivery, ensuring systematic data collection, analysis, and customized report generation.

### Pipeline Stages
1. **Promotion & Lead Generation**
2. **Lead Development & Data Enrichment**
3. **Business Profiling Survey**
4. **Employee Survey Distribution**
5. **Data Collection & Follow-up**
6. **Data Processing & Analysis**
7. **Document Generation**
8. **Delivery & Follow-up**

## Stage 1: Promotion & Lead Generation

### Channels
- **Content Marketing**: Blog posts, white papers, case studies
- **Social Media**: LinkedIn articles, Twitter threads, Facebook posts
- **Email Marketing**: Newsletter campaigns, targeted outreach
- **Speaking Engagements**: Webinars, conferences, podcasts
- **Paid Advertising**: LinkedIn Ads, Google Ads
- **Partnerships**: Technology vendors, industry associations

### Lead Capture
- **Landing Page**: Dedicated page with service overview and call-to-action
- **Contact Form**: Simple form requesting basic information
- **Consultation Scheduler**: Calendly integration for booking calls
- **Lead Magnet**: Free AI readiness checklist or assessment

## Stage 2: Lead Development & Data Enrichment

### Initial Contact
1. **Automated Welcome Email** (immediately after form submission)
   - Thank you message
   - What to expect next
   - Calendar link for discovery call

2. **CRM Entry**: Create lead record with source information
   - Company name, industry, size
   - Contact person and role
   - Lead source and campaign
   - Initial notes and observations

### Data Enrichment
1. **Company Research**
   - Website analysis
   - LinkedIn company page
   - Industry reports and news
   - Financial information (if available)
   - Technology stack indicators

2. **Contact Enrichment**
   - LinkedIn profile analysis
   - Professional background
   - Industry connections
   - Previous experience with AI

## Stage 3: Business Profiling Survey

### Survey Delivery
- **Email with Survey Link**: Personalized email with survey link
- **Follow-up Schedule**:
  - Day 0: Initial email
  - Day 3: First follow-up
  - Day 7: Second follow-up
  - Day 14: Final follow-up

### Survey Content
- Company information
- Technical infrastructure
- Business processes
- Organizational readiness
- Goals and expectations
- Challenges and concerns

### Response Tracking
- **Survey Platform**: Google Forms, SurveyMonkey, or Typeform
- **Response Dashboard**: Real-time response tracking
- **Completion Rate**: Monitor and optimize
- **Follow-up Triggers**: Automated reminders for incomplete surveys

## Stage 4: Employee Survey Distribution

### Key Employee Identification
- **Business Development**: Sales/Marketing leaders
- **Operations**: Operations/Production managers
- **Technology**: IT/Technical staff
- **Finance**: Finance/Accounting personnel
- **Customer Service**: Customer support leaders

### Survey Distribution
1. **Email to Primary Contact**
   - Request employee contact information
   - Explain purpose and confidentiality
   - Provide survey links for each employee

2. **Individual Emails**
   - Personalized survey invitation
   - Clear instructions and timeline
   - Confidentiality assurance
   - Contact information for questions

### Follow-up Escalation
- **Day 3**: Reminder email to non-respondents
- **Day 7**: Second reminder with escalation notice
- **Day 10**: Final notice with copy to primary contact
- **Day 14**: Survey closed, analysis based on responses received

## Stage 5: Data Collection & Follow-up

### Response Collection
- **Survey Platform Dashboard**: Monitor responses in real-time
- **Automated Notifications**: Email alerts for new responses
- **Response Export**: Regular data exports for analysis
- **Data Validation**: Check for completeness and consistency

### Follow-up Escalation Process
1. **Level 1**: Automated email reminders
2. **Level 2**: Personal follow-up from account manager
3. **Level 3**: Escalation to primary contact with explanation
4. **Level 4**: Final notice and survey closure

### Data Quality Assurance
- **Completeness Check**: Ensure all required fields completed
- **Consistency Validation**: Cross-reference with other responses
- **Outlier Detection**: Identify unusual or inconsistent responses
- **Data Cleaning**: Standardize and normalize data formats

## Stage 6: Data Processing & Analysis

### Data Integration
1. **Survey Data Consolidation**
   - Business profile survey responses
   - Employee survey responses (aggregated)
   - Company research data
   - CRM and enrichment data

2. **Data Storage**: Centralized database or spreadsheet
   - All responses in structured format
   - Cross-references between data sources
   - Version control for data files

### Analysis Process
1. **Data Cleaning & Preparation**
   - Remove incomplete responses
   - Standardize data formats
   - Handle missing data appropriately
   - Create unified dataset

2. **Statistical Analysis**
   - Descriptive statistics (means, medians, frequencies)
   - Correlation analysis between different areas
   - Trend identification across departments
   - Gap analysis between current and desired states

3. **Qualitative Analysis**
   - Open-ended response coding
   - Theme identification
   - Pain point categorization
   - Opportunity recognition

4. **Comparative Analysis**
   - Compare responses across departments
   - Compare leadership vs. employee perspectives
   - Benchmark against industry standards
   - Identify alignment and misalignment

### Problem Area Identification
1. **Technical Gaps**
   - Infrastructure limitations
   - Data quality issues
   - Integration challenges
   - Security concerns

2. **Process Inefficiencies**
   - Manual bottlenecks
   - Error-prone activities
   - Time-consuming workflows
   - Lack of standardization

3. **Organizational Challenges**
   - Skills gaps
   - Cultural resistance
   - Change management issues
   - Resource constraints

4. **Strategic Misalignment**
   - Goals vs. capabilities
   - Vision vs. reality
   - Short-term vs. long-term focus
   - Leadership vs. employee perspectives

## Stage 7: Document Generation

### Template System
- **Strategy Document Template**: Comprehensive strategic plan
- **Implementation Plan Template**: Detailed action plan
- **PowerPoint Overview Template**: Executive presentation
- **Cover Letter Template**: Personalized introduction

### Customization Process
1. **Data Integration**
   - Extract key findings from analysis
   - Incorporate specific company data
   - Use actual survey responses as examples
   - Reference specific pain points and opportunities

2. **Content Generation**
   - **Executive Summary**: Key findings and recommendations
   - **Current State Analysis**: Detailed assessment of current situation
   - **Opportunity Identification**: AI use cases and potential applications
   - **Implementation Roadmap**: Phased approach with timelines
   - **Risk Assessment**: Potential challenges and mitigation strategies
   - **ROI Analysis**: Expected benefits and financial impact
   - **Success Metrics**: KPIs and measurement approach

3. **Document Assembly**
   - Populate templates with customized content
   - Add company-specific examples and case studies
   - Include relevant industry benchmarks
   - Ensure consistent branding and messaging

### Quality Assurance
- **Review Process**: Multiple review stages for accuracy
- **Consistency Check**: Ensure all documents align
- **Customization Verification**: Confirm all content is specific to client
- **Professional Formatting**: Polished, professional appearance

## Stage 8: Delivery & Follow-up

### Delivery Package
1. **Email Delivery**
   - Personalized cover letter
   - Strategy document attachment
   - Implementation plan attachment
   - PowerPoint overview attachment
   - Additional resources (checklists, templates)

2. **Delivery Format**
   - PDF documents for easy sharing
   - Editable formats (Word, PowerPoint) for client use
   - Online dashboard for interactive exploration
   - Presentation option for executive review

### Follow-up Process
1. **Initial Follow-up** (2-3 days after delivery)
   - Confirm receipt of documents
   - Schedule feedback call
   - Address any immediate questions

2. **Implementation Support**
   - Regular check-in calls
   - Additional clarification as needed
   - Referrals to implementation partners
   - Ongoing advisory support

3. **Long-term Relationship**
   - Quarterly business review
   - Update assessments as needed
   - Referral program for new business
   - Expansion opportunities

## Tools & Technology

### Survey Tools
- **Primary Survey Platform**: SurveyMonkey, Typeform, or Google Forms
- **Response Management**: Automated response tracking
- **Analytics Dashboard**: Real-time response monitoring

### CRM & Pipeline Management
- **CRM System**: HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive
- **Pipeline Tracking**: Visual pipeline management
- **Automation**: Workflow automation for follow-ups
- **Reporting**: Performance metrics and analytics

### Document Generation
- **Template System**: Document assembly software
- **Content Library**: Pre-written content blocks
- **Customization Tools**: Text editors, formatting tools
- **Quality Control**: Review and approval workflows

### Communication Tools
- **Email Marketing**: Mailchimp, ConvertKit, or similar
- **Calendar Scheduling**: Calendly or similar
- **Video Conferencing**: Zoom or Teams
- **Project Management**: Asana, Trello, or ClickUp

## Metrics & KPIs

### Pipeline Metrics
- **Lead Conversion Rate**: Leads to discovery calls
- **Discovery Call to Proposal Rate**: Calls to proposals
- **Proposal to Close Rate**: Proposals to clients
- **Average Project Value**: Revenue per project
- **Sales Cycle Length**: Time from lead to close

### Survey Metrics
- **Response Rate**: Business survey completion
- **Employee Participation**: Number of employee surveys completed
- **Follow-up Effectiveness**: Response rate after escalation
- **Data Quality**: Completeness and consistency

### Delivery Metrics
- **On-Time Delivery**: Projects delivered on schedule
- **Client Satisfaction**: Post-delivery feedback
- **Document Quality**: Accuracy and customization level
- **Repeat Business Rate**: Client retention and expansion

## Continuous Improvement

### Feedback Loops
- **Client Feedback**: Post-delivery surveys and interviews
- **Process Review**: Monthly pipeline performance review
- **Template Updates**: Regular template improvements
- **Skill Development**: Ongoing training and education

### Optimization Opportunities
- **Automation**: Identify manual processes for automation
- **Template Enhancement**: Improve customization and quality
- **Delivery Speed**: Reduce time from lead to delivery
- **Client Experience**: Enhance overall client journey

This pipeline provides a systematic approach to delivering high-quality, customized AI readiness consulting services while maintaining efficiency and scalability.
